title: What to Do First After Being Laid Off
subtitle: A step-by-step survival checklist from the day of notification to months of transition
summary: The administrative, legal, and financial actions required when terminated or laid off. Arranged chronologically from the hour before signing to months after.

items.text: If the company hands you a form stating "Voluntary Resignation for Personal Reasons," do not sign it. Signing usually wipes out both statutory economic severance (N) and unemployment insurance claims.

If management urges you to "sign first so HR can process it, severance will follow," demand severance terms be written directly into the severance agreement on the spot. If omitted, refuse to sign; you face zero legal penalty for refusing to sign on day one.

Turn on audio recording when entering a severance meeting. In India you may record a conversation you are part of, and a genuine recording can be used as evidence; do not record a conversation you are not part of.
Before handing back your laptop and account access, back up pay stubs, attendance records, employment contracts, social security statements, and key chat records.
Only preserve evidence directly proving your labor relationship. Never download or take proprietary company source code, customer directories, or technical design documents.
Hand over all administrative credentials and permissions cleanly. Do not delete data, alter passwords, or tamper with systems, even if the employer owes you wages.

sections.heading: Day 1 to the First Few Days: Calculate the Money

items.text: Calculate your statutory severance (N): 1 month of wages for every full year of service. Any period over 6 months counts as 1 year; any period under 6 months pays half a month.

Monthly salary must be calculated from your true average total compensation across the past 12 months, including performance bonuses, allowances, and subsidies. This is the figure employers most commonly manipulate downward.

Clarify the exact statutory clause used for termination. Notice pay (+1 month) is legally mandated in only 3 scenarios where 30 days prior written notice was not given: medical inability after sickness period, competence failure after training/reassignment, or fundamental change in objective conditions. Economic layoffs or mutual separations do not require +1 month.

If termination is unlawful under labor contract law, compensation is 2N (double severance). Consult a lawyer or free legal aid hotline (12348) to confirm unlawful termination status before deciding between settlement or arbitration.
Settle unused annual statutory leave pro-rated for the portion of the year already worked.
Itemize and demand any accrued unpaid overtime pay before finalizing the termination receipt.
Register for unemployment immediately. Unemployment benefits are calculated starting from the registration date; delaying by a month costs you a full month of payments.
Complete unemployment registration at public employment service centers; public agencies charge zero fees.

Apply for monthly unemployment insurance via the "Handheld 12333" App or electronic social security card mini-program. You are eligible if premiums were paid for at least 1 year and departure was involuntary.
While receiving unemployment insurance, your basic employee medical insurance is covered directly by the unemployment fund without paying out of pocket.
If litigation costs are prohibitive, call 12348 to apply for state-funded legal aid. You no longer need to travel to your registered hometown for poverty certificates.

Retain original non-compete agreements. The former employer must pay monthly compensation; if they fail to pay for 3 consecutive months due to employer fault, you may request termination of the non-compete.
Anchor a strict daily routine: wake at regular hours, block dedicated time for job applications, and avoid remaining isolated at home all day.
If wages or severance are withheld, lodge a complaint with the Labor Inspection Bureau via 12333 before filing labor arbitration. Both channels are completely free.
Even if employed by an unlicensed workshop or contractor, labor inspection and arbitration still apply. For general contractors vs subcontractors, hold the general contractor liable.
Labor arbitration must be formally filed within 1 year of termination. Once the 1-year statute of limitations expires, the employer can dismiss claims simply by citing the time bar.
Use public employment agencies for verified job placement and resume clinics; steer clear of commercial agencies demanding advance recruitment fees.
Instantly reject offers demanding "pay fee before onboarding", "mandatory training before placement", or multi-level referral recruiting.
Check the municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau's official subsidized vocational skills catalogue before enrolling in paid training classes.
Cover ongoing daily living expenses strictly from your liquid emergency reserve fund; do not take high-interest consumer credit or liquidate long-term investments at a loss.

Postpone major irreversible decisions for at least 3 months: selling property, investing entire severance sums into new businesses, entering speculative partnerships, or guaranteeing third-party loans.

If unemployment benefits expire before finding work, maintain medical coverage by paying resident medical insurance independently on an annual basis to avoid the 3-month reimbursement waiting period upon lapse.
Pension contributions never zero out upon interruption; historical years accumulate permanently. Never spend money paying fraudulent intermediary agencies for fake employer affiliations.
If distress becomes overwhelming, dial the free national crisis counseling line 12356.

title: Right After Being Diagnosed with a Chronic Illness
subtitle: What to do in your first week, first three months, and subsequent maintenance years
summary: A time-ordered checklist for those newly diagnosed with hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, or gout. Focuses on concrete actions, cost-saving state policies, and long-term organ preservation.

items.text: If the diagnosis is severe, have a trusted companion accompany you when picking up reports. Defer major life disruptions like resigning or selling real estate.
If medication is prescribed, start immediately and do not stop when symptoms temporarily subside.
Blood pressure and cholesterol medications must be taken consistently every single day; never halt them independently.
Purchase an upper-arm electronic blood pressure monitor, measure regularly at home, and bring values down to clinical targets.
When having prescriptions filled, proactively ask the physician for bioequivalent generic drugs selected under national centralized bulk procurement (centralized bulk procurement).
For newly diagnosed Type 2 diabetes, undergo an immediate dilated fundus eye examination. Type 1 diabetes should begin annual screening 5 years after onset.
For confirmed gout, initiate continuous uric acid-lowering therapy to maintain serum urate below 360 µmol/L permanently.
People of Southeast Asian ancestry, and anyone with kidney disease, should ask their doctor about HLA-B*5801 testing before starting allopurinol to reduce the risk of a severe skin reaction.
If a routine health check shows high uric acid without any prior inflammatory gout flares, do not start urate-lowering drugs without medical evaluation.
Smokers must set a firm cessation date and quit entirely in one attempt rather than tapering.

tipRef.label: Set a definitive smoking cessation day

items.text: Do not rely solely on sheer willpower to quit smoking; seek prescription pharmacotherapy from hospital smoking-cessation outpatient clinics.
Maintain a dedicated physical health notebook: record the date, laboratory indicators, medication names, and exact dosages at every follow-up visit.

tipRef.label: Log chronic markers in one notebook

items.text: Archive personal copies of all outpatient medical records, laboratory sheets, and diagnostic imaging scans.

tipRef.label: Keep copies of reports and imaging

items.text: Register for Outpatient Chronic & Serious Disease Reimbursement Status (outpatient chronic disease designation) in your insurance district. If consulting doctors in other cities, complete cross-regional medical filing.
If family members hold formal employee basic medical insurance, bind Family Mutual-Aid Sharing (family mutual-aid account sharing) to allow their personal account balance to pay for your medications.
When signing with a community family doctor, verify in advance which specific services are covered by public insurance versus out-of-pocket.
Replace household table salt with low-sodium potassium salt (unless renal impairment or potassium-sparing medications are present).
Walk 7,000–8,000 steps daily or accumulate 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity brisk walking every week.
Minimize or completely eliminate alcohol consumption.
Never suspend validated medical therapy to experiment with unverified folk remedies, health tonics, or herbal supplements.
When purchasing cold or pain medications, verify ingredients to ensure paracetamol (acetaminophen) is present in only one single formulation to prevent liver failure.
Once clinical parameters stabilize, request 12-week long prescriptions at community health service centers in one visit.
For diabetic patients, perform an annual neurological foot examination and dilated eye screening at recommended intervals.

tipRef.label: Annual diabetic foot and eye checks

items.text: Kidney stone patients should maintain a fluid intake of 2.5 to 3.0 liters per day and reduce sodium consumption under 6 grams.
Individuals with cardiovascular conditions must receive an annual influenza vaccination every autumn.
Always consult community tier-1 hospitals first; when hospital admission is necessary, utilize tiered hierarchical referral to retain deductible carry-over.
Each ascending hospital grade lowers public insurance reimbursement by approximately 10 percentage points within the same municipal pool.

title: Administrative Tasks Before and After Childbirth
subtitle: A chronological guide to records, birth registration, insurance claims, and vaccines
summary: A complete administrative timeline spanning prenatal hospital establishment, birth certification, newborn medical insurance, and mandatory childhood immunizations.

items.text: Complete hospital prenatal establishment (maternity record establishment) in early pregnancy to lock in delivery beds at designated maternity hospitals.
Supplement 400 micrograms of folic acid daily starting before conception through the end of the first trimester to prevent neural tube defects.
Complete Down syndrome screening or non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) at designated gestational weeks.
Confirm active status of your employer maternity insurance (maternity insurance) to qualify for full medical fee reimbursement and statutory paid maternity leave allowance.
Ensure both parents have original national ID cards and marriage certificates ready for the issuance of the Medical Birth Certificate (Medical Birth Certificate).
Carefully confirm the child's official legal name before the certificate is printed; changing names later on household registration requires police administrative approval.
Ensure the newborn receives initial Hepatitis B and BCG vaccinations prior to hospital discharge and obtain the official Vaccination Certificate (Vaccination Certificate).
Register the infant's birth with the local municipal registrar, using the birth certificate and the parents' identity and address proof.

Enroll the infant in Urban and Rural Resident Basic Medical Insurance (Resident Basic Medical Insurance) within 90 days of birth to enable retroactive reimbursement of birth-related hospital expenses.

tipRef.label: Newborn resident medical insurance within 90 days

items.text: Apply for the child's physical Social Security Card at a designated bank or government public service center.
Submit the formal maternity allowance (maternity allowance) claim via the provincial HR & Social Security platform.
Strictly follow the National Immunization Program (Category 1 free vaccines) schedule at your community health center.
Prioritize key self-funded Category 2 vaccines with strong evidence: 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine and rotavirus vaccine.
Maintain safe sleep practices: place infants on their back to sleep on a firm mattress with zero pillows, loose blankets, or soft toys to eliminate SIDS risks.

title: Family Emergency Equipment & Preparedness Checklist
subtitle: The essential hardware, food, first aid, and documentation for home crises
summary: A practical, non-paranoid inventory of household emergency supplies covering clean water, shelf-stable nutrition, power, illumination, trauma care, and vital paper documents.

items.text: Store 3 liters of commercially bottled drinking water per person per day (a minimum of 9 to 10 liters per individual for a standard 72-hour emergency).

tipRef.label: 3L drinking water per person per day

items.text: Keep shelf-stable, ready-to-eat foods that do not require refrigeration or cooking: compressed energy biscuits, canned meats, and vacuum-sealed nuts.
Keep a manual, non-electric rotary can opener next to stored canned goods.
Equip a dedicated first aid kit: sterile pressure bandages, medical tourniquet, adhesive dressings, nitrile gloves, and povidone-iodine disinfectant swabs.

tipRef.label: Home trauma and wound first aid kit

items.text: Maintain a minimum 2-to-4 week rolling reserve of daily essential prescription medications for family members with chronic illnesses (blood pressure, insulin, cardiac drugs).
Stock oral rehydration salts (ORS III) and basic antipyretics (paracetamol / ibuprofen) with strict adherence to single-ingredient guidelines.
Keep an AM/FM emergency radio with hand-crank and solar backup charging to receive civil defense announcements when cell towers collapse.
Store high-lumen LED flashlights and spare rechargeable batteries kept stored at 70%–80% charge level.
Maintain high-capacity power banks recharged quarterly and keep standard charging cables for all household devices in the emergency bag.
Provide fire evacuation filter hoods (certified 30-minute toxic gas smoke filtering) for every family member kept near bedroom exits.
Keep heavy-duty heat-resistant work gloves for handling debris, shattered glass, or hot surfaces during an evacuation.
Equip each grab-bag with high-decibel pealess whistles for signaling rescuers without depleting vocal stamina.
Store physical cash in small denominations (¥10, ¥20, and ¥50 banknotes) in waterproof bags; card readers, cellular point-of-sale terminals, and QR code payments fail during grid collapses.
Keep waterproof sealed pouches containing physical copies of identity cards, birth and marriage certificates, property deeds, and medical cards.

title: Checklists Before Changing Jobs or Relocating Cities
subtitle: Financial calculations, commute thresholds, social insurance portability, and non-competes
summary: A rigorous evaluation methodology for evaluating new job offers, comparing net living compensation across cities, preserving insurance continuity, and avoiding contractual traps.

items.text: Calculate your actual social security and housing fund contribution base. Many employers promise high gross salaries while reporting the minimum legal baseline, drastically diminishing true total compensation.

tipRef.label: Verify true social security contribution base

items.text: Deconstruct variable annual bonuses: evaluate historical payout rates and ascertain whether bonus terms are formally codified in the contract or left to unilateral management discretion.
Calculate true hourly wage factoring in mandatory uncompensated overtime, transit times, and expected weekend work.
Set an absolute hard ceiling of 45 minutes for one-way commute times; longer daily commutes significantly increase chronic stress, hypertension, and sleep deficit.
When moving cities, factor in initial cash outlays: apartment deposits (usually deposit plus three months' rent upfront), agency commission, and relocation logistics.
Verify whether rental utility billing is calculated at residential municipal rates or commercial tier rates.

Scrutinize non-compete agreements. In India, a clause that restrains you from working after your employment ends is generally void under section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; confidentiality and non-solicitation clauses can still be enforced.
Never download or transfer proprietary source code, internal repositories, or client records when transitioning between employers.
Ensure the previous employer issues an official Termination Certificate (Termination Certificate) promptly, as the new employer requires it to complete lawful onboarding.
Initiate inter-provincial pension account transfers via the national 12333 social security portal after establishing your new employment relationship.
Coordinate medical insurance transition carefully to ensure coverage does not lapse beyond 3 months, which triggers a reset of reimbursement waiting periods in many municipalities.
Transfer your Housing Provident Fund (Housing Provident Fund) balance via the national Housing Provident Fund Mini-Program after 6 months of continuous deposits in the destination city.

title: Circadian Rhythms, Shift Work, and Health Preservation
subtitle: Mitigating cardiovascular, metabolic, and cognitive harm from irregular work hours
summary: Evidence-based strategies for shift workers, overnight personnel, and frequent travelers to stabilize circadian clocks, protect sleep architecture, and reduce long-term morbidity.

sections.heading: Biological Principles of Circadian Disruption
prose: The human circadian pacemaker resides in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the hypothalamus, synchronized primarily by optical light exposure. Melatonin synthesis by the pineal gland is profoundly suppressed by short-wavelength blue spectrum light.

Chronic circadian misalignment from erratic shift work is classified as a probable human carcinogen and significantly elevates long-term risks of cardiovascular disease, Type 2 diabetes, and depression.

items.text: Permanent fixed night shifts cause substantially less circadian turbulence than erratic, constantly rotating shifts.

When rotating schedules are unavoidable, insist on clockwise forward rotation (Day shift -> Evening shift -> Night shift -> Rest), allowing natural phase delays rather than punishing counter-clockwise shifts.
Wear high-grade polarized sunglasses during your morning commute home after an overnight shift to prevent sunlight from resetting your morning circadian clock.

tipRef.label: Wear sunglasses on morning commute home

items.text: Install 100% total blackout curtains in your bedroom; even minimal ambient daylight penetration significantly degrades slow-wave sleep quality.
Use custom-fit silicone earplugs and soundproofing to isolate against daytime domestic and traffic disturbances.
Concentrate caffeine consumption during the initial first half of the work shift; cut off all caffeine intake at least 6 hours prior to your target sleep window.
Avoid heavy high-glycemic carbohydrates during overnight shifts; consume light, protein-focused meals to maintain glucose stability without inducing postprandial somnolence.
Conduct annual fasting blood glucose, lipid panel, and blood pressure monitoring to catch metabolic shifts early.

title: The Legal and Economic Calculus of Marriage
subtitle: Analyzing property rights, debt exposure, risk pooling, and divorce statutes under the Civil Code
summary: A factual analysis of the legal and financial mechanisms established by civil marriage. Covers pre-marital assets, joint debts, estate inheritance, and property titling.

sections.heading: What Marriage Is in the Eyes of the Law
prose: Legally speaking, marriage is an economic partnership contract defined by the Civil Code. It automatically links property rights, debt liabilities, inheritance claims, and fiduciary care obligations between two individuals.
Entering marriage without understanding its legal framework creates substantial unintended exposure to liabilities, shared debt risks, and protracted property division.

items.text: Assets owned prior to marriage (bank balances, vehicles, real estate titled solely in one party's name before marriage) remain individual separate property and do not automatically convert to joint property through time.
Income earned during marriage (salaries, business revenues, investment yields, housing fund contributions) belongs jointly to both spouses regardless of who earned more.

Real estate bought prior to marriage with a personal down payment but amortized jointly with post-marital income belongs to the titled purchaser upon divorce, but the other spouse is entitled to full compensation for the amortized capital and proportional market appreciation.

Under Article 1064 of the Civil Code, debts incurred jointly by both spouses or ratified retroactively are joint debts. Debts incurred by one spouse exceeding normal household family needs are individual debts unless the creditor proves they benefited the family.
Never sign as a co-borrower or guarantor for a spouse's commercial business loans or speculative ventures unless you intend to assume unlimited personal joint liability.

sections.heading: The Economic Balance Sheet: Pros vs Cons

rows: High: mutual legal obligation to support during catastrophic illness or disability
Zero: individual self-reliance and commercial insurance buffers
Parental care deduction sharing, family health insurance mutual aid
Complex statutory division, 30-day cooling-off period, potential litigation
Clean separation of individually held accounts and titles
Primary first-order statutory heir with statutory right to estate
No automatic statutory inheritance without explicit will

title: What Licenses and Permits Are Needed to Run an Online Platform
subtitle: From basic ICP filing to EDI commercial permits, public security records, and multi-tier cybersecurity protection
summary: A structured regulatory guide for developers, founders and engineers operating internet services in India. Covers intermediary duties, data protection, payments and sector licences.

sections.heading: Core Regulatory Requirements for Every Website

items.text: Intermediary duties: India does not require an ICP filing. A platform that hosts user content should publish terms of use, appoint a grievance officer, and follow the IT Rules, 2021 to keep its safe harbour under section 79 of the IT Act, 2000.

Data protection: If you process personal data, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires a lawful basis, a notice and reasonable security safeguards. A significant data fiduciary has additional duties.
Domain Real-Name Verification: Domain names must be authenticated through approved domestic registrars; failure to complete real-name verification blocks DNS resolution.
Commercial ICP License (Value-Added Telecom Permit - B25): Legally required if the platform charges users for access to digital content, paywalled articles, or paid subscriptions.
EDI License (B21 Online Data Processing): Mandated when operating a multi-vendor marketplace where third-party merchants transact with consumers.
Classified Cybersecurity Protection (MLPS Level 2 / Level 3): Platforms collecting large-scale user datasets must undergo formal graded evaluation by accredited security testing institutions.
Online Cultural Business Permit (Online Cultural Operation Permit): Required if publishing anime, comics, games, or streamed music.
Internet Drug Information Service Qualification: Mandatory before publishing any medical or pharmaceutical information, even for non-commercial education.

title: Encountering a Stranger in Trouble: Walk Away or Stop and Help?
subtitle: A cost-benefit breakdown across legal liability, bystander risks, and emergency procedures
summary: An objective analysis of the three courses of action when encountering an injured stranger or sudden collapse in public. Details Civil Code Article 184 protections and defensive evidence protocols.

rows: Fully legal under PRC law (no statutory duty for ordinary citizens to rescue strangers)
Low (phone number is logged with dispatch)
Highest (immediate physical proximity before cameras verified)

sections.heading: Legal Protections: Motor Vehicles Act section 134A
prose: Under section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a Good Samaritan who helps a road-accident victim in good faith shall not be liable for any civil or criminal action for any injury or harm caused while rendering emergency care.
The protection reduces the legal risk of helping, but it does not remove the need to report the accident and to give a truthful account to the police.

sections.heading: Defensive Action Protocols for Good Samaritans

items.text: Turn on video recording on your smartphone before stepping forward, capturing the surrounding context, ambient scene, and visible witnesses.
Loudly recruit adjacent bystanders: "Let us call 120 together and look after this person together" to eliminate single-witness vulnerability.
Never move or drag an injured stranger suspected of spinal or cervical trauma unless there is an imminent peril of explosion, building collapse, or road traffic.
If the individual is in cardiac arrest, perform chest compressions or retrieve an automated external defibrillator (AED) immediately.
